deadline-driver.title: C1b: bounded native observation and verified delivery

pitfalls.failure: UIA provider does not return by its deadline
pitfalls.recovery: Use admitted Win32/MSAA controls; resolve new fallback tokens. No desktop-root search or process cleanup.

pitfalls.failure: A dispatched action times out
pitfalls.recovery: Do not send another action. Wait for its native lane to finish and verify actual state before a deliberate retry.

pitfalls.failure: Input desktop differs from the process desktop
pitfalls.recovery: Background actions require the isolated native driver and an input-desktop attribution guard. Foreground input is disabled; an unavailable guard refuses launch or action.

pitfalls.failure: Field protection metadata is missing or a field became disabled/read-only
pitfalls.recovery: Unknown metadata refuses unbound fields. A token-labelled, job-owned disposable document has its own file identity scope; known password, disabled and read-only fields still refuse. Never infer ownership from an old token.

frontier: C1b breadth, atomic latency and active-desktop preservation are proven by C11g on local disposable targets; its 3 historical guard-failure records are retained and the whole-session guard flag stays false, so a passing final run does not erase them
Real UIA cached-pattern/event-diff, general MSAA traversal and T18 model fallback require their own native runs. Isolated native SendInput is disabled.
T18 image-to-CL remains the existing explicit visual adaptation route; this change proves bounded PrintWindow capture, not an automatic model decision.

A Bureau launch needs a unique new window, token ownership and verified membership on a noncurrent virtual desktop before action admission. Windows may refuse Shell view registration for contained windows; this is an isolation-unavailable frontier, not missing owner permission. Never show a window on the input desktop or reuse an existing singleton to bypass it.

C11f (nine apps, four learned flows) is superseded by C11g (15 apps). C11g re-enables visibility diagnostics and proves inactive Bureau placement on Explorer Default even when input is Screen-saver. Calculator CoreWindow lacks injected hook coverage and is refused; shared broker adoption and general Office rendered preview remain unproven. The 15 apps are COM/headless application-native flows plus private UIA/CDP on local disposable targets; that is not universal pixel interaction, and apps that reject background messages keep their native refusal.
guidance: Windows discovery uses EnumWindows and skips IsHungAppWindow. A persistent in-process MTA UIA client uses ConnectionTimeout 50 ms and TransactionTimeout 80 ms.
Every UIA/MSAA call runs in a single bounded lane. A busy lane rejects new work immediately; no growing worker pool or PowerShell action process.
Target-scoped CacheRequest snapshots keep properties and patterns. Property events update cached nodes; structure events refresh only their changed branch. Event buffering is bounded.
Isolated native routing uses cached UI Automation patterns, admitted background native messages or MSAA. Foreground input and SendInput are disabled regardless of session flags.
Paul's physical input remains independent of isolated native actions. Explicit preview Take over pauses this session; Give back resumes it with the user's note.
Observation source, nativeRevision, nativeDiff and degradedReason describe the actual route. Win32 readback and application file effects establish native results.
No new public command: existing cua.inspect/action/verify/adapt/flow and preview APIs use the same NativeWorker facade. cycle is an internal benchmark/native operation.

Create a fresh task-local target whose path contains a random 32-character hexadecimal token. launch_app args may include disposable_target {path,token}; the driver binds it only after independent new-window job/desktop ownership and an observed token in its title. Existing broker windows cannot be adopted by this argument.

Fresh Chrome, Edge and VS Code profiles may expose a task-reserved CDP endpoint on an explicit owned port. The DOM route verifies the local document URL or the token-bearing VS Code page before every evaluation, changes real fields, dispatches their application events and reads fresh values. It never attaches to a user's profile or sends desktop input.

The native fallback projects actual SysTreeView32 items and owned menu commands. Tree expansion and selection use bounded native messages and fresh affected-item readback; MSAA tree/list roles remain distinct from generic controls.

The active task panel is config/cua-everyday-tasks.json. It excludes system administration; older frozen panels are historical receipts only. Use disposable notes, generated images, documents and local files.

Brokered installed binaries have an explicit Bureau route, suspended job launch and a before-launch HWND inventory. Admit only new owned HWNDs with verified noncurrent membership; never adopt an existing user window or activate an uncontained alias. Explorer /n receives a token-named disposable folder and /separate; shared broker HWND ownership remains unproven.
Notepad skips when an existing instance could reuse a user window. Paint and Calculator use installed binaries and a new owned process; a hidden launch does not prove Bureau membership.

Office tasks use a new hidden COM instance with PID/birth ownership and save/reopen/package checks. Registered neyvia.nativeapp.open/edit/persist/observe/close drive the native-applications manual. Three grounded runs feed manual.compile; replay uses manual.script.run with fresh checks and zero model tokens. These are application-native tool flows, not UIA or pixel workflows.

scripts/prove_c11f_shell.py performs actual CREATE_NO_WINDOW file tasks with independent file and ZIP readback. It cannot change system configuration. C11f.json records these lanes separately from the native manual-compiler cohort.

Bureau uses Explorer Default, not the current input desktop, which can be Screen-saver. The guard observes both desktops continuously. Private desktop windows need no lease. Only a new owned HWND receives one nonrenewable move lease, capped at three seconds.

New Bureau windows are held hidden before launch resumes. Token-bearing documents must finish loading before admission. Registration stays offscreen with native focus vetoes; pixels reach normal bounds only after actual target GUID membership and DWM Shell cloak are independently verified. DeleteTab is forbidden after placement because it destroys the Shell view and membership.

Preview images are immutable by advertised sequence and capture identity. The pane swaps loaded pixels and their metadata together. Coordinates and forwarded input use the displayed frame; expired frames and foreign windows refuse. Identical pixels may retain earlier semantic controls, but each selected control is freshly validated before dispatch.

Preview scroll resolves the observed scrollable ancestor. Classic owned ListBox scroll uses bounded WM_VSCROLL and fresh LB_GETTOPINDEX effect readback. A degraded observation may be retried as a read only; an uncertain dispatched action is never retried.

cua.action.pre: Active session whose allow-list holds the target app; Paul has not taken over; element_token comes from the latest inspect of that window (snapshot-bound) or x,y are pixels of a capture_id

cua.wait.effect: Block until Paul gives control back (or timeout); returns his give-back note and every action he did in the preview meanwhile
cua.wait.pre: Use after a paused_by_user refusal or when you asked Paul to try something

cua.log.effect: Read the shared log (agent and Paul): who, tool, element, ActionResult, approvals, notes
cua.log.pre: Session exists; since_seq from a previous next_seq to read only what is new

pane.show.effect: Open the live preview on Paul's stage: the window, the element you act on outlined before each action, the shared log, Take over/Give back and the allow-list
pane.show.pre: kind preview; target is the session id, or empty for the newest active session

set-field-and-verify.goal: Show the owned preview, inspect and review one field, resolve it afresh, set and independently verify its value

right-element.constraints: Tokens are snapshot-bound: use only tokens from the latest inspect of this window. If two elements share the label, pick by role and position or ask Paul. Never act on a window Paul did not allow.
right-element.question: Is the element token the field the task means (role, label and position in the inspect result), in an allowed app?

pitfalls.failure: effect refused, error.code paused_by_user
pitfalls.recovery: Paul took over in the preview. Call neyvia.cua.wait; read his note and paulActions; continue from the new state, do not repeat old steps blindly

pitfalls.failure: effect refused, error.code app_not_allowed
pitfalls.recovery: Ask with launch_app (creates an approval) or tell Paul in chat which app and why; never work around the allow-list

pitfalls.failure: effect refused, error.code background_unavailable
pitfalls.recovery: The target drops background input. Try an observed UI Automation pattern or admitted native message. Isolated native foreground delivery and SendInput remain disabled; report the actual refusal.

pitfalls.failure: effect refused, error.code stale_element_token
pitfalls.recovery: The window changed. Inspect again and take the token from the new snapshot

pitfalls.failure: effect unverifiable or suspected_noop
pitfalls.recovery: Neither failure nor success. Verify with neyvia.cua.verify or a fresh inspect before moving on

pitfalls.failure: effect refused, error.code denied_by_user or approval_timeout
pitfalls.recovery: Paul said no (or was away) to an irreversible action. Do not retry the same action; explain in chat and pick a reversible path

pitfalls.failure: Frame shows minimized or protected
pitfalls.recovery: The driver cannot see minimized or capture-protected windows; ask Paul to restore it, never un-minimize with foreground tricks

frontier: Canvas and custom-drawn surfaces with no UI Automation peer can only be driven by pixel clicks on a capture; the driver has no OCR (the AGPL perception extension is never used)
Isolated native sessions ignore Paul's independent physical input. Preview Take over pauses this session explicitly.
guidance: Contract: plans/15-handoff.md ## T16 (Session, Frame, LogEntry, refusal codes). Tool shape: trycua/cua libs/cua-driver contract/manifest.json and docs/action-result-contract.md.
MCP agents use the same session through python -m grant_agent.neyvia_cua_mcp with cua-driver's tool names (click, type_text, get_window_state, ...); Neyvia models use neyvia.cua.*.
Snapshot before every action: inspect, act with a token from that inspect, verify. Prefer element tokens over coordinates.

In CL use cua.windows(), then cua.inspect(w1), then cua.action(tool="set_value", args={element:e1, value:"text"}). The host fills the driver token and binds value-is to the observed window, role, label and requested value. element_token:e1 is also accepted; literal tokens and stale or foreign refs are refused. Author G from cua.verify before mutation; unsupported observer checks remain frontier.
User side: pane.show preview (web/src/neyvia/next/NxPreviewPane.jsx) shows the window, outlines the element before each action, and lists every action of yours and Paul's.

Connected Language: inspect with diff_only=true returns a full window state and handle first; pass previousHandle for scoped changes. reset=true requests a new full state. Handles remain bound to this session and window.
C11 background work uses UI Automation patterns or admitted PostMessage on the agent desktop. Preview input uses this same driver; browser input in headless proof does not inject Windows input.

Zero-disturbance proof attributes foreground changes and visible windows to agent process trees, and requires zero LLMHF_INJECTED mouse events and zero LLKHF_INJECTED keyboard events on the input desktop. Paul's independent activity does not invalidate the run.

Flow step args.observation_timeout_ms accepts 0..10000 milliseconds for bounded read-only initialization and fresh protection observations. Missing/unknown observations may retry; ambiguity refuses immediately. Verification requires two adjacent fresh satisfied observations. No mutation is retried.

open-on-agent-desktop.goal: Launch an allowed app on the private agent desktop and confirm Paul's desktop saw no foreground, window or injected-input change

click-and-verify.goal: In the selected private window, click the named button and verify the field's resulting value

pitfalls.failure: launch refused with isolated_launch_unavailable or app_not_allowed
pitfalls.recovery: Brokered, Store or singleton apps (Notepad, Calculator, Paint on Windows 11) have no proven private route; ask Paul for an allowed classic app, never a visible launch

pitfalls.failure: cua.windows lists untitled helper windows next to the app
pitfalls.recovery: Select the titled main window with cua.inspect(wN) before each procedure; a procedure acts on the window of the latest observation

pitfalls.failure: typed-value or composed-value is unsatisfied
pitfalls.recovery: Inspect again and read the field's actual value; the app decides where a click inserts (Character Map's Select inserts at the caret). Do not repeat the click blindly

frontier: Proven on Character Map (classic Win32) through the authenticated backend, CL procedures, an independent separate-process WM_GETTEXT readback and the agent-view time-lapse (scripts/prove_rx_cua_journey.py). Saving a document through a private-desktop file dialog is not yet proven.

The proven journey's task is issued through neyvia.cl on the owner's HTTP route. prove_rx_cua_journey.py --arm claude gives the same task to a Claude Code chat whose only tools are Neyvia's computer-use MCP; that arm has not completed yet (the local Claude CLI sign-in had expired).
guidance: Journey: run cua.open-on-agent-desktop(path=...), then cua.windows() and cua.inspect(wN) on the titled window, run cua.type-and-verify(...), cua.inspect(wN) again (an action retires the previous observation), then run cua.click-and-verify(...). Every action sits behind a check; the desktop guard is part of the launch check.
Paul allows the app for the chat first (preview allow-list); the chat identity of an owner HTTP CL call is http-owner:<session>.
The agent view mirrors the session: every action gets an 'after' keyframe in the time-lapse at /api/ui/agentview/timeline.
